column8: Mon 16 Nov: 2.5 could-not-show clause: by Perold's own words a simulator is the paper book, so 2.5 claims completeness and fees, never low slippage; adds the paper quote to Q17-001's frame.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the Value Line gap shows the shortfall grows with turnover, a weekly stock picker unlike a ladder bought and held; at most one clause in 3e.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.5's five-line cost account (fees $200, NUMBERS 8g; taxes out of scope; impact none; opportunity cost $0); say spreads were not shown by WInS, never not charged, since how WInS fills (bid, offer or last) is UNVERIFIED (row 1).
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q17-001 (the targets at decision prices as Perold's paper book); carry the wish-list quote and the caution that the Portfolio tab was exported 14 Oct, after the fills.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q17-001's two parts; Perold's Appendix B read only through Hendershott et al.; the $0 opportunity cost is carried by Q88-033.
Mon 16 Nov: benchmark detail for Q17-001; keep its wording rule for 2.5: against the prices the targets were set on, never against the market.
Mon 16 Nov: restates Q17-001/Q17-002 (the standard measure); carry CFA Institute (2026a) as the citation a Wharton judge knows, and its closing-price benchmark for books valued at the close.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; most of the sheet-to-fill gap is delay (targets on 2 Oct closes, orders 6-7 Oct ET), market movement not execution; Wagner and Edwards' 0.20% is secondary only, do not cite it.

Mon 16 Nov: arithmetic checked ($507.48 + $50.10 = $557.58 against portfolio.csv and the snapshot), but the figure is not in NUMBERS 8m; register it before use, never as money saved (Wharton: WInS gains are never evidence; 8b: luck of timing).

Mon 16 Nov: supports aha 3 (built to need the year, not the day), but the contrast sets six funds' fills against the model value of the ten, not like for like; date 7 Oct as a US close with fills 6-7 Oct ET; $558 is not in NUMBERS.

Mon 16 Nov: $200 against $200 matches NUMBERS 8g and tickets.md, but a fixed fee always meets its estimate and tests nothing; it is the cost-against-estimate line of Q88-033's spine, said plainly and claimed for nothing.

Mon 16 Nov: arithmetic on 8g checks (2.6, 10.7-12.6, 5.2-6.7, 9.4, 6.7 bp), but only 6.7 bp is in NUMBERS 8m and SKELETON keeps 2.5 in dollars; at most a Table 1 note or 2.1's what does not scale, after registering.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.5's VT 167 / 164 clause with a reason a judge can check: price drift landed in VT and cash, never in the ten Treasury holdings bought at exact target units (8m), beside TNA l.23; $476.49, $558.79 and the sheet's $2,955 are not in NUMBERS 8m, so register them or say it without figures.

Mon 16 Nov: the completion line is the first item of Q88-033's spine; 2.5 already leads with it (Q29-012, NUMBERS 8m); keep its caution that four orders were cancelled and placed again, so completion counts filled trades.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; the regulator's arrival benchmark needs the bid and offer at each order, which WInS did not keep, so any ETF spread figure in 2.5 is an estimate from published medians (Q17-035).

Mon 16 Nov: Table 3 check at the Jan 2028 build and the 2031 move (price against NAV and the 30-day median spread); IPS l.13's whichever works best is about T-bond or fund, so do not hang this check on it; never a new IPS rule.

Mon 16 Nov: re-checked at Treasury's methodology page today (indicative, bid-side quotations, not actual transactions, most recently auctioned securities, New York Fed at or near 3:30 PM); 2.5: why the bond check is a band, not a point; label 2.6-8.8 bp as MODEL (8m).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and 2.5: no public trade tape exists for the old bonds Laura will buy (FINRA 6750 publishes on-the-run coupons only), so the public curve is her yardstick; a strong limit stated as a fact.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e: a Treasury confirmation prints no markup (Rule 2232 excludes Treasuries, SEC 34-79346), so the cost sits in the price and the curve check is the only check she can make herself; pairs with Q88-018.

Mon 16 Nov: re-checked at source (JF 2013: average 3.61 bp, peak 20.47 on 10 Dec 2008, bonds 1-10 years, root mean squared distance); 2.5's band: about seven times normal scatter and above the average at the 2008 peak; never every genuine price would have passed in 2008 (20.47 is an average across bonds, one bond can stray further); cite the JF version, the NBER paper gives 3.32.

Mon 16 Nov: re-checked at source (17 CFR 240.15c3-5(c)(1)(i)-(ii), (c)(2)(ii)); 2.5 buying it: the five stop rules on file (tickets.md, Q29-013) are the controls a US broker must run before an order reaches the market; the rule binds brokers, so say same kinds of check, never compliance.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.5: names the curve band as FMSB's first test, a staleness and error filter on the one quote WInS showed, not a cost measure; it caught the two stale screen prices (SKELETON 2.5: 111 and 92 bp).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the professional bond benchmark is a paid evaluated price neither WInS nor Laura's broker shows, so 2.5 says checked against the Treasury curve, never best execution.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.5 may say each bond was checked against the curve before its order (5 Oct, -10 to +6 bp), but the 2.6-8.8 bp at the fills is Q17's MODEL measured after the freeze (8m: measured afterwards, labelled so), never a second check the team made at the time.
Mon 16 Nov: store, 3e: with one broker (Q78) Laura gets no competing quotes, so the curve check stands in for competition; the 23.7 bp is the manager's own claim.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; the escrow broker-fee safe harbour ($3,000 on $300,000 before cost-of-living rises) is an issuer's admin-cost rule, not a market price, so it answers is $200 a lot only loosely.

Mon 16 Nov: updates Q17-035's $250 with bond half-spreads (about $277, 0.09%), but it is not in NUMBERS; drop the one number a practitioner would accept; cite 0.07% as data from a withdrawn 2023 SEC proposal, never a rule; WInS spread charge is UNVERIFIED, not absent; Table 1 note only.

Mon 16 Nov: citation hygiene for Q45-026 and Q88-027: the SEC withdrew Regulation Best Execution (Release 33-11377), so the 0.07% is SEC staff data from a withdrawn proposal, never an SEC rule or standard.
Mon 16 Nov: another authority for Q17-001's name (Keim and Madhavan, most natural method); adds nothing CFA (2026a) does not.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.5's close (Book 17, evaluate): measuring is for improving, so end on what the build changed for January 2027 (the curve check before every order; one person placing orders after the mis-click, told without attribution); abstract only.
Mon 16 Nov: performance holiday is the same point as Q88-032 (a build is judged by cost and completion, returns count only after); carry the term and Laura's three builds (NUMBERS 8r) as a clause.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.5: the build is measured to the last fill and nothing after, the profession's own rule and Wharton's (no 23 Oct value, no return); one clause that answers why 2.5 reports no gain.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.5's order in a filed report's spine: completion, cost against estimate, the driver of the one difference (VT 167 / 164), then how it was bought; carries rows 11 and 14; source not re-checked today (site refused), card's reading stands.
Mon 16 Nov: a filed example of Q17-003's point (market moves swamp execution: 168 of 206 bp was opportunity cost); keeps $200 apart from the $37,625 swing (8b) for aha 3.

Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q29-026/Q29-027 (a model portfolio's results are hypothetical); never call the WInS book a model portfolio, since our trade notes use that phrase for the plan the book is scaled to (CANON A18).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e limits and 2.5's could-not-show; $75-$105 is a plan figure not in NUMBERS; two-thirds scale is banned in prose (SKELETON 2.0: say $300,000 of the plan's $450,000); SKELETON keeps 2.5's could-not-show to the 2028 date, so dealer costs go to 3e.
